name: Ram-pump water purifier
subtitle: a stream's force pushes water through a filter

effects.effect: a moving liquid stopped suddenly sends a sharp pressure spike along its pipe
small molecules seep through a membrane

effect: a moving liquid stopped suddenly sends a sharp pressure spike along its pipe
how: Many hill villages have a stream but no clean water and no power to run a purifier. Water rushing down a pipe is slammed shut by a valve many times a minute; each sudden stop throws a pressure spike many times normal (water hammer), and those spikes push part of the water through a fine membrane that holds back germs and dissolved salts.
obstacle: Membranes are built for steady pressure, and repeated spikes could tear or clog them quickly.
why: Clean water with no fuel, no electricity and one moving part.
real: A 2002 Desalination paper argues water hammer from a hydro-ram can supply reverse-osmosis pressure, and a HeroX concept proposes a ram-pump-fed RO system; no tested prototype found.
